```{r setup}
## ============================================================================
## first_results_database.qmd: first preliminary report on the database (ANALYSIS_SPEC §6)
## Assembles the D and A outputs of one pass with comments. Reads the saved tables and figures
## of analysis/output/{run_date}/ only and computes nothing new: the only arithmetic is sums,
## medians, minima and maxima of saved values. Definitions in the boxes come from docs/GLOSSARY.md.
## Render (Quarto bundled with RStudio):
##   quarto render analysis/qmd/first_results_database.qmd --output-dir ../output/2026-11-02
## ============================================================================

source(here::here("analysis", "paths.R"))   # dir_tables, dir_figures, run_date

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)


## --- Helpers: read a saved output, pick one value, format ---
read_table <- function(name, ...) {
  f <- file.path(dir_tables, paste0(name, ".csv"))
  if (!file.exists(f)) stop("Saved table not found: ", f)
  read.csv(f, ...)
}

## Figures are referenced by a path relative to this qmd, so that embed-resources finds them
fig_path <- function(name, ext = "png") {
  f <- file.path(dir_figures, paste0(name, ".", ext))
  if (!file.exists(f)) stop("Saved figure not found: ", f)
  xfun::relative_path(f, dir = getwd(), use.. = TRUE)
}

## One value from a saved table: stop() unless the filter selects exactly one row
val <- function(df, column, ...) {
  x <- df %>% filter(...) %>% pull(all_of(column))
  if (length(x) != 1) stop("val(): ", length(x), " rows selected for ", column)
  x
}

pct  <- function(x, digits = 0) paste0(formatC(100 * x, format = "f", digits = digits), "%")
num  <- function(x) prettyNum(x, big.mark = ",")   # element by element, so integers stay integers
pint <- function(x, lo, hi) paste0(pct(x), " [", round(100 * lo), ", ", round(100 * hi), "]")   # share with 95% interval

## "a, b and c"
and_list <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) <= 1) return(x)
  paste(paste(x[-length(x)], collapse = ", "), "and", x[length(x)])
}

```

::: {.callout-warning title="Status of these results"}
```{r status}
## Law year per country (Table A1): the latest text in the corpus, never one year for all
law_year_min    <- min(table_a1$law_year_max)
law_year_max    <- max(table_a1$law_year_max)
alloc_not_high  <- val(table1, "value", item == "share with alloc_ai_confidence not high")
instr_not_high  <- val(table1, "value", item == "share with instr_ai_confidence not high")
```

- **Preliminary.** These results come before the validation of ANALYSIS_SPEC §4 (recall, precision and κ, stability, corpus completeness), which must come before any institutional result is written up.
- **Coverage.** `r n_countries` countries (Eritrea, Mauritania, Somalia, South Sudan and Sudan are not covered). De jure: the tables describe what the law assigns, not what is collected or spent. One cross-section, no census of instruments, so no prevalence.
- **Law year.** Each country is described by the law in force as of the latest text in its corpus. That year differs by country (from `r law_year_min` to `r law_year_max`) and is given per country in Table A1 (`law_year_max`, `law_year_median`).
- **AI confidence.** `r pct(alloc_not_high)` of top-level allocations and `r pct(instr_not_high)` of instruments are coded with less than high confidence (pooled).
- **Not in this report.** A5 (reform candidates) is deferred to a later project. The regression check of A7 (predicted shares by design group) is held back for review. Section B (external data: WoRLD, GRD, PEFA) comes in a second report.
- **Pass.** Tables and figures of the pass of `r run_date`, read from `analysis/output/`; nothing is recomputed here.
:::


# Descriptive overview (D)

::: {.callout-note title="How to read this"}
An **instrument** is one charge (tax, levy, fee, fine) whose proceeds the law assigns somewhere; a *class placeholder* stands for a class of charges the law names without listing them. An **allocation** is one assignment of an instrument's proceeds to one destination; the **top level** is the first split of the gross proceeds.

*Unit:* stated in each row. *Set:* every instrument in the database (all E-classes, social contributions included).
:::

```{r d1}
## Table 1 as saved; shares shown as percentages, means with one decimal
n_instruments  <- val(table1, "value", item == "instruments")
n_documents    <- val(table1, "value", item == "documents read")
n_placeholders <- val(table1, "value", item == "row_kind class_placeholder")
n_e3 <- val(table1, "value", item == "earmark_class E3")
n_e2 <- val(table1, "value", item == "earmark_class E2")
n_e4 <- val(table1, "value", item == "earmark_class E4")
n_e1 <- val(table1, "value", item == "earmark_class E1")
share_unallocated <- val(table1, "value", item == "share of restricted allocations with cofog_division = unallocated")

table1_show <- table1 %>%
  mutate(is_share = grepl("^share", unit),
         value  = ifelse(is_share, pct(value, 1), num(value)),
         across(c(country_mean), ~ ifelse(is.na(.x), "", formatC(.x, format = "f", digits = 1))),
         across(c(country_median, country_min, country_max), ~ ifelse(is.na(.x), "", num(.x)))) %>%
  select(-is_share)

kable(table1_show, col.names = c("Item", "Unit", "Total", "Mean per country", "Median", "Min", "Max"),
      align = "llrrrrr", caption = "Table 1. The database at a glance")
```

The database holds `r num(n_instruments)` instruments and classes of charges in `r n_countries` countries, coded from `r num(n_documents)` documents. Per country, the number of instruments runs from `r val(table1, "country_min", item == "instruments")` to `r val(table1, "country_max", item == "instruments")` (median `r val(table1, "country_median", item == "instruments")`). E3 is the largest class with `r num(n_e3)` instruments, followed by E2 (`r num(n_e2)`) and E4 (`r num(n_e4)`); the E1, E4 and E0 counts are incidental, because they count only the instruments the corpus happens to assign in those ways. Class placeholders are `r num(n_placeholders)` instruments (`r pct(n_placeholders / n_instruments)`), and `r pct(share_unallocated, 1)` of restricted top-level allocations have no COFOG division.

Appendix Table A1 gives the same counts and the four design shares for each country.


# Analysis on the database (A)

## A1. How much earmarking, and where?

::: {.callout-note title="How to read this"}
The **earmarked set** is E2 + E3: instruments with at least one restricted destination. E3 (exclusive) sends all proceeds to restricted destinations, apart from small collection-cost shares; E2 (partial) sends part to the general budget.

*Unit:* instrument (left panel); allocation, top level, restricted legs, a pool counted once (right panel). *Set:* earmarked, social contributions excluded. Shares are country-equal.
:::

```{r a1}
n_earmarked   <- sum(a1$n_earmarked)
n_alloc_restr <- sum(a1$n_alloc_top_restricted)
a1_min <- a1 %>% filter(n_earmarked == min(n_earmarked))
a1_max <- a1 %>% filter(n_earmarked == max(n_earmarked))
e3_min <- a1 %>% filter(E3_share == min(E3_share))
e3_max <- a1 %>% filter(E3_share == max(E3_share))
```

```{r a1-fig, fig.cap = "A1. Earmarked instruments and restricted allocations, by country"}
include_graphics(fig_path("02_A1_countries"))
```

The earmarked set holds `r num(n_earmarked)` instruments and classes of charges, with `r num(n_alloc_restr)` restricted top-level allocations. Per country, it runs from `r min(a1$n_earmarked)` instruments (`r and_list(cname(a1_min$country))`) to `r max(a1$n_earmarked)` (`r and_list(cname(a1_max$country))`), with a median of `r median(a1$n_earmarked)`. These counts depend on corpus completeness and on how each legal system splits charges, so we compare countries by shares within the earmarked set.

The E3 share has a median of `r pct(median(a1$E3_share))` across countries. It runs from `r pct(min(a1$E3_share))` in `r and_list(cname(e3_min$country))` to `r pct(max(a1$E3_share))` in `r and_list(cname(e3_max$country))`. Across countries, the median fund-or-agency share is `r pct(median(table_a1$fund_agency_share))`, the median hard-commitment share `r pct(median(table_a1$hard_commitment_share))` and the median benefit-linked share of links `r pct(median(table_a1$benefit_linked_share))` (Table A1).


## A2. What finances earmarks, and what do they finance?

::: {.callout-note title="How to read this"}
A **link** is one instrument × one COFOG division it finances, through restricted assignments only; heatmaps, Sankeys and benefit links count links. **Base groups** are 12 groups of what is taxed (ANALYSIS_SPEC §2). Links are counts of legal assignments, not revenue.

*Unit:* link (A2a, A2c); allocation (A2b); instrument (A2d). *Set:* earmarked, social contributions excluded. Shares are country-equal unless stated.
:::

### A2a. Source × function heatmap

```{r a2a}
## Shares of links by division: sum of the saved cell shares over base groups
a2a_division <- a2a %>%
  group_by(cofog_division) %>%
  summarise(n_links = sum(n_links), share_country_equal = sum(share_country_equal), .groups = "drop")
n_links_total <- sum(a2a_division$n_links)
if (abs(sum(a2a_division$share_country_equal) - 1) > 1e-6) stop("A2a: division shares do not sum to 1")
share_704 <- val(a2a_division, "share_country_equal", cofog_division == "704")
second_division <- a2a_division %>%
  filter(!cofog_division %in% c("704", "unallocated")) %>%
  slice_max(share_country_equal, n = 1)
top_cells <- a2a %>% arrange(desc(n_links)) %>% slice(1:3)
n_unallocated <- val(a2a_division, "n_links", cofog_division == "unallocated")
```

```{r a2a-fig, fig.cap = "A2a. Base group × COFOG division: number of links (label: number of countries)"}
include_graphics(fig_path("02_A2a_heatmap"))
```

Of the `r num(n_links_total)` links, division 704 Economic affairs receives `r pct(share_704)` (`r num(val(a2a_division, "n_links", cofog_division == "704"))` links). The next division is `r cofog_labels[second_division$cofog_division]`, with `r pct(second_division$share_country_equal)`. The largest cell is `r tolower(base_labels[top_cells$base_group[1]])` × 704, with `r top_cells$n_links[1]` links in `r top_cells$n_countries[1]` countries, followed by `r tolower(base_labels[top_cells$base_group[2]])` × 704 (`r top_cells$n_links[2]`) and `r tolower(base_labels[top_cells$base_group[3]])` × 704 (`r top_cells$n_links[3]`). Another `r n_unallocated` links (`r pct(val(a2a_division, "share_country_equal", cofog_division == "unallocated"))`) have no COFOG division.

### A2a′. Zoom on 704 Economic affairs

```{r a2a-zoom}
## Shares of the 704 pairs by COFOG group: sum of the saved cell shares over base groups
zoom_group <- a2a_zoom %>%
  group_by(cofog_group) %>%
  summarise(n_pairs = sum(n_pairs), share_country_equal = sum(share_country_equal), .groups = "drop")
zoom_top_group <- zoom_group %>% slice_max(share_country_equal, n = 1)
zoom_empty     <- zoom_group %>% filter(n_pairs == 0)
zoom_cells     <- a2a_zoom %>% arrange(desc(n_pairs)) %>% slice(1:4)
cell_text <- paste0(tolower(base_labels[zoom_cells$base_group]), " × ", zoom_cells$cofog_group,
                    " (", zoom_cells$n_pairs, ")")
```

```{r a2a-zoom-fig, fig.cap = "A2a′. Base group × COFOG group within 704: number of instrument × group pairs"}
include_graphics(fig_path("02_A2a_zoom704"))
```

Within 704, `r cofog704_labels[zoom_top_group$cofog_group]` has the largest share of pairs (`r pct(zoom_top_group$share_country_equal)`, `r zoom_top_group$n_pairs` pairs). The four largest cells pair a base group with the COFOG group of the same sector: `r and_list(cell_text)`. `r and_list(cofog704_labels[zoom_empty$cofog_group])` has no pair and is left out of the figure. An instrument that finances two 704 groups counts in both.

### A2b. Recipient forms

```{r a2b}
n_alloc_a2b <- sum(a2b$n_allocations)
a2b_ordered <- a2b %>% arrange(desc(share_country_equal))
```

```{r a2b-fig, fig.cap = "A2b. Recipient forms of restricted top-level allocations"}
include_graphics(fig_path("02_A2b_recipient_form"))
```

Agencies receive `r pct(val(a2b, "share_country_equal", recipient_form == "agency"))` of the `r num(n_alloc_a2b)` restricted top-level allocations and funds `r pct(val(a2b, "share_country_equal", recipient_form == "fund"))`. Programmes or purposes follow with `r pct(val(a2b, "share_country_equal", recipient_form == "program_or_purpose"))` and special accounts with `r pct(val(a2b, "share_country_equal", recipient_form == "special_account"))`. All `r min(val(a2b, "n_countries", recipient_form == "agency"), val(a2b, "n_countries", recipient_form == "fund"))` countries have at least one allocation to an agency and one to a fund. These are legal forms as written: a fund is anything the law calls a fund, which says nothing about its budget status.

### A2d. Instrument types

```{r a2d}
a2d_show <- a2d %>%
  arrange(desc(share_country_equal)) %>%
  transmute(type = type_labels[instrument_type], n_instruments, n_countries,
            country_equal = pct(share_country_equal, 1), pooled = pct(share_pooled, 1))
if (val(a2b, "n_countries", recipient_form == "agency") != 43 || val(a2b, "n_countries", recipient_form == "fund") != 43) stop("A2b: agency or fund not in every country")
if (any(is.na(a2d_show$type))) stop("A2d: instrument_type without a label")
a2d_max_gap <- max(abs(a2d$share_country_equal - a2d$share_pooled))

kable(a2d_show, col.names = c("Instrument type (GFS)", "Instruments", "Countries", "Country-equal share", "Pooled share"),
      align = "lrrrr", caption = "A2d. Instrument types of earmarked instruments")
```

Fines and penalties are the largest type of earmarked instrument (`r pct(val(a2d, "share_country_equal", instrument_type == "fine_penalty"))`), followed by administrative fees (`r pct(val(a2d, "share_country_equal", instrument_type == "administrative_fee"))`) and use-permission taxes (`r pct(val(a2d, "share_country_equal", instrument_type == "use_permission_tax"))`). Taxes on broad bases are few: income and profits taxes are `r pct(val(a2d, "share_country_equal", instrument_type == "income_profits_tax"), 1)` and general consumption taxes `r pct(val(a2d, "share_country_equal", instrument_type == "general_consumption_tax"), 1)`. Country-equal and pooled shares differ by at most `r round(100 * a2d_max_gap, 1)` percentage points. These are shares of the earmarked set, not shares of all charges in force.

### A2c. One Sankey per country

```{r a2c}
## Main-text countries (provisional) and the reason for each choice, from 03_sankey_candidates.csv
sankey_main <- sankey_candidates %>% filter(main_text) %>%
  mutate(design_group = factor(design_group, levels = design_main)) %>% arrange(design_group)
if (nrow(sankey_main) != 4) stop("A2c: expected 4 main-text countries, found ", nrow(sankey_main))
tie_zmb <- sankey_candidates %>% filter(country == "SWZ")
tie_cpv <- sankey_candidates %>% filter(country == "AGO")
for (iso in sankey_main$country) fig_path(paste0("03_A2c_sankey_", iso))   # stop() if a figure is missing
```

::: {.callout-note title="How to read the Sankeys"}
Flows go from base group (left) to COFOG division (right) and count links, not revenue. The five base groups with the most links (pooled, the catch-all services group excluded) have their own colour in every country; the others are grey. Node order is the same in every country. *Unit:* link. *Set:* earmarked, social contributions excluded.
:::

We show one country per main design group, the one whose number of links is closest to its group median: `r cname(sankey_main$country[1])` for UEMOA (`r sankey_main$n_links[1]` links, median `r sankey_main$group_median_links[1]`), `r cname(sankey_main$country[2])` for CEMAC (`r sankey_main$n_links[2]`, median `r sankey_main$group_median_links[2]`), `r cname(sankey_main$country[3])` for anglophone countries (`r sankey_main$n_links[3]`, median `r sankey_main$group_median_links[3]`) and `r cname(sankey_main$country[4])` for lusophone countries (`r sankey_main$n_links[4]`, median `r sankey_main$group_median_links[4]`). Two choices break ties around the median. `r cname("ZMB")` is preferred to `r cname(tie_zmb$country)` for its lower class placeholder share (`r pct(val(sankey_candidates, "placeholder_share", country == "ZMB"))` against `r pct(tie_zmb$placeholder_share)`), and `r cname("CPV")` to `r cname(tie_cpv$country)` because it adds a non-resource-intensive country to three resource-rich ones. The choice is provisional.

::: {.panel-tabset}
```{r a2c-tabs, results = "asis"}
## One tab per main-text country; the line under each figure reads 03_sankey_flows.csv
for (i in seq_len(nrow(sankey_main))) {

  flows_c <- sankey_flows %>% filter(country == iso)

      " (", largest$n_links, " links).\n\n", sep = "")
}
```

## A3. Is there an economic rationale?

::: {.callout-note title="How to read this"}
Each link gets one **benefit link**, tested in this order. *Corrective*: the destination mitigates the harm the base causes. *Compensatory*: it compensates the territory bearing the activity. *Benefit*: it serves the payers themselves. *Sectoral*: it serves the taxed sector as a whole. *General revenue*: a broad base with no specific link. *Unlinked*: a specific base and an unrelated destination.

*Unit:* link (links with no COFOG division excluded). *Set:* earmarked, social contributions excluded. Shares are country-equal.
:::

```{r a3}
a3_all <- a3 %>% filter(group == "all countries")
a3_share <- function(link, grp = "all countries") val(a3, "share_country_equal", group == grp, benefit_link == link)
n_links_a3 <- sum(a3_all$n_links)
n_null_a3  <- unique(a3_all$n_null_excluded)
```

```{r a3-fig, fig.cap = "A3. Benefit link of earmark links, overall and by legal family"}
include_graphics(fig_path("02_A3_benefit_link"))
```

Sectoral links are the largest class (`r pct(a3_share("sectoral"))` of `r num(n_links_a3)` links), followed by benefit (`r pct(a3_share("benefit"))`) and unlinked (`r pct(a3_share("unlinked"))`) links. Corrective links are `r pct(a3_share("corrective"))`, general revenue links `r pct(a3_share("general_revenue"))` and compensatory links `r pct(a3_share("compensatory"))`. The unlinked share is `r pct(a3_share("unlinked", "francophone_civil"))` in francophone civil law countries and `r pct(a3_share("unlinked", "anglophone_common"))` in anglophone common law countries. The `r n_null_a3` links with no COFOG division are left out.

```{r a3-table}
a3_show <- a3 %>%
  mutate(group_label = paste0(ifelse(group == "all countries", "All countries", family_labels[group]),
                              " (", countries_in_mean, ")")) %>%
  select(group_label, benefit_link, share_country_equal) %>%
  mutate(share_country_equal = pct(share_country_equal),
         benefit_link = factor(benefit_link, levels = names(benefit_labels))) %>%
  arrange(benefit_link) %>%
  mutate(benefit_link = benefit_labels[as.character(benefit_link)]) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = group_label, values_from = share_country_equal)

kable(a3_show, col.names = c("Benefit link", names(a3_show)[-1]), align = "lrrrrrr",
      caption = "A3. Share of links in each class, country-equal, by legal family (number of countries in brackets)")
```

The hispanophone group is one country (Equatorial Guinea) and the mixed group two (Rwanda and Ethiopia), so their shares are not group comparisons.


## A4. How binding are earmarks?

::: {.callout-note title="How to read this"}
**Commitment strength.** *Hard*: a fixed share to a dedicated body or account, in a law voted by parliament. *Firm*: a fixed share routed through a ministry or programme, or written only in an annual finance law. *Soft*: a share left to a later decree, unstated or bounded, or an assignment made by decree. An instrument's commitment is its strongest assignment.

*Unit:* instrument (E-class, commitment); allocation, top level, restricted legs, a pool counted once (vehicle, legal rank, determinacy). *Set:* earmarked, social contributions excluded. Shares are country-equal.
:::

```{r a4}
a4i <- function(cat, grp = "all countries") val(a4_instrument, "share_country_equal", group == grp, category == cat)
a4a <- function(meas, cat) val(a4_allocation, "share_country_equal", group == "all countries", measure == meas, category == cat)
```

```{r a4-fig, fig.cap = "A4. Commitment strength of earmarked instruments, by legal family"}
include_graphics(fig_path("04_A4_commitment"))
```

E3 instruments are `r pct(a4i("E3"))` of the earmarked set and E2 instruments `r pct(a4i("E2"))`. The strongest commitment of an instrument is hard for `r pct(a4i("hard"))`, soft for `r pct(a4i("soft"))` and firm for `r pct(a4i("firm"))`. The hard share is `r pct(a4i("hard", "francophone_civil"))` in francophone civil law countries and `r pct(a4i("hard", "anglophone_common"))` in anglophone common law countries.

```{r a4-table}
a4_show <- a4_allocation %>%
  filter(group == "all countries") %>%
  transmute(measure = recode(measure, vehicle_class = "Vehicle", legal_rank = "Legal rank", determinacy = "Determinacy"),
            category = gsub("_", " ", category), n, n_countries,
            country_equal = pct(share_country_equal, 1), pooled = pct(share_pooled, 1))

kable(a4_show, col.names = c("Measure", "Category", "Allocations", "Countries", "Country-equal share", "Pooled share"),
      align = "llrrrr", caption = "A4. Restricted top-level allocations of earmarked instruments: vehicle, legal rank and determinacy (all countries)")
```

Of restricted top-level allocations, `r pct(a4a("vehicle_class", "fund_or_agency"))` go to a fund-or-agency vehicle, `r pct(a4a("vehicle_class", "on_budget"))` to an on-budget vehicle and `r pct(a4a("vehicle_class", "territorial_external"))` to territorial or external bodies. `r pct(a4a("legal_rank", "ordinary_law"))` sit in an ordinary law, `r pct(a4a("legal_rank", "regulation"))` in a regulation and `r pct(a4a("legal_rank", "finance_law"))` in a finance law; this describes where the clauses sit in the corpus. `r pct(a4a("determinacy", "determinate"))` of allocations state a determinate share and destination.


## A6. Sharing with local governments and regional bodies

::: {.callout-note title="How to read this"}
Each allocation to or through a subnational tier has one **type of sharing**: general tax sharing (a share of a national tax paid into a tier's budget, free to use), specific tax sharing (the use is restricted), devolved earmark, equalisation transfer, derivation transfer, or functional earmark of a tier's body. Sharing allocations are also split into restricted and unrestricted. Administrative retentions (collection costs, payments to local collectors or chiefs) are never sharing: they are counted apart and left out of the types and the figure.

*Unit:* sharing allocation to or through a subnational tier, all share levels, a pool counted once (administrative retentions counted apart). *Set:* assigned (E1 + E2 + E3), social contributions excluded. Counts only.
:::

```{r a6}
a6_n_alloc  <- sum(a6_country$n_allocations)
a6_n_instr  <- sum(a6_country$n_instruments)
a6_with     <- a6_country %>% filter(n_allocations > 0)
a6_none     <- a6_country %>% filter(n_allocations == 0)
if (a6_n_alloc != sum(a6_incidence$n_allocations)) stop("A6: by-country and incidence totals differ")
## Sharing allocations only (05_territorial.R, decision of 2 Nov 2026); retentions are one separate count
if (sum(a6_country$n_restricted + a6_country$n_unrestricted) != a6_n_alloc) stop("A6: restricted + unrestricted do not sum to the sharing allocations")
a6_n_ret <- sum(a6_country$n_retention)
if (!all(grepl(paste0("excludes ", a6_n_ret, " "), a6_incidence$note))) stop("A6: the incidence note does not match the retentions of the by-country table")
a6_type <- function(type, column) val(a6_incidence, column, assignment_type == type)
retention_max <- a6_country %>% slice_max(n_retention, n = 1)
```

```{r a6-fig, fig.cap = "A6. Subnational sharing allocations by type of sharing, by country"}
include_graphics(fig_path("05_A6_subnational"))
```

The law assigns `r num(a6_n_alloc)` sharing allocations of `r num(a6_n_instr)` instruments to or through subnational tiers, in `r nrow(a6_with)` countries; `r and_list(cname(a6_none$country))` have none. Of these allocations, `r num(sum(a6_country$n_unrestricted))` are unrestricted and `r sum(a6_country$n_restricted)` restricted; `r sum(a6_country$n_below_top)` sit below the top level. General tax sharing is the most common type (`r a6_type("tax_sharing_general", "n_allocations")` allocations in `r a6_type("tax_sharing_general", "n_countries")` countries), followed by derivation transfers (`r a6_type("derivation_transfer", "n_allocations")` in `r a6_type("derivation_transfer", "n_countries")`).

We report administrative retentions separately, because they are never sharing. The law assigns `r a6_n_ret` of them at the subnational level (`r retention_max$n_retention` in `r cname(retention_max$country)`): collection costs and payments to local collectors or chiefs. They are not in the figure or in the table of types.

These counts reflect the type of decentralisation, not its degree. Tax sharing written into tax codes appears as allocations, whereas grants set each year do not, and annual revenue-division Acts were excluded from the corpus.

```{r a6-table}
a6_show <- a6_incidence %>%
  transmute(type = sharing_labels[assignment_type], n_allocations, n_countries) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_allocations))
if (any(is.na(a6_show$type))) stop("A6: assignment_type without a label")

kable(a6_show, col.names = c("Type of sharing", "Allocations", "Countries"), align = "lrr",
      caption = "A6. Subnational sharing allocations by type of sharing (administrative retentions excluded)")
```

**Regional bodies.** `r a6_regional$n_allocations` allocations in `r a6_regional$n_countries` countries go to a supranational body. They are recorded only where a national text restates the levy, because community acts were not collected.


## A7. Do legal traditions shape the design?

::: {.callout-note title="How to read this"}
**Design groups**: UEMOA francophone, CEMAC francophone, francophone outside the CFA zone, anglophone, lusophone outside the CFA zone. Guinea-Bissau and Equatorial Guinea (CFA, not francophone) and Rwanda and Ethiopia (mixed) are labelled points, never groups. UEMOA and CEMAC against non-CFA francophone countries is the harmonisation contrast; anglophone against non-CFA francophone countries is the legal-tradition contrast.

*Unit:* allocation (a); country (b). *Set:* earmarked, social contributions excluded. Group comparisons are associations, not effects.
:::

### A7(a). Recipient forms by design group

```{r a7a}
a7a_main <- a7a %>% filter(level == "design_group", group %in% design_main)
a7a_share <- function(grp, form) val(a7a_main, "share_country_equal", group == grp, recipient_form == form)
## Check of the text: agencies and funds are the two largest forms in each of the five main groups
a7a_top2 <- a7a_main %>% group_by(group) %>% slice_max(share_country_equal, n = 2) %>% ungroup()
if (!all(a7a_top2$recipient_form %in% c("agency", "fund")) || nrow(a7a_top2) != 10) stop("A7(a): agency and fund are not the top two everywhere")
a7a_af <- a7a_main %>% filter(recipient_form %in% c("agency", "fund")) %>%
  group_by(group) %>% summarise(share = sum(share_country_equal), .groups = "drop")
a7a_af_franco <- a7a_af %>% filter(group %in% c("uemoa_francophone", "cemac_francophone", "francophone_noncfa"))
```

```{r a7a-fig, fig.cap = "A7(a). Recipient forms of restricted top-level allocations, by design group"}
include_graphics(fig_path("04_A7a_recipient_form"))
```

Agencies and funds are the two largest recipient forms in each of the five main groups. Together they take `r pct(val(a7a_af, "share", group == "anglophone_common"))` of restricted top-level allocations in anglophone countries, against `r pct(min(a7a_af_franco$share))` to `r pct(max(a7a_af_franco$share))` in the three francophone groups. Special accounts take `r pct(a7a_share("uemoa_francophone", "special_account"))` in UEMOA, `r pct(a7a_share("cemac_francophone", "special_account"))` in CEMAC and `r pct(a7a_share("francophone_noncfa", "special_account"))` in non-CFA francophone countries, against `r pct(a7a_share("anglophone_common", "special_account"))` in anglophone countries. These are legal forms as written, not budget status.

### A7(b). Design profile

```{r a7b}
a7b_med <- function(meas, grp) val(a7b_groups, "median", measure == meas, design_group == grp)
a7b_main <- a7b_groups %>% filter(design_group %in% design_main)
hard_other <- a7b_main %>% filter(measure == "hard_commitment_share", design_group != "anglophone_common")
benefit_main <- a7b_main %>% filter(measure == "benefit_linked_share")
e3_main <- a7b_main %>% filter(measure == "E3_share")
e3_low  <- e3_main %>% slice_min(median, n = 1)
e3_high <- e3_main %>% slice_max(median, n = 1)
```

```{r a7b-fig, fig.cap = "A7(b). Design profile: country shares and group medians"}
include_graphics(fig_path("04_A7b_profile"))
```

Group medians of the E3 share run from `r pct(e3_low$median)` in `r design_prose[e3_low$design_group]` to `r pct(e3_high$median)` in `r design_prose[e3_high$design_group]`. The median hard-commitment share is `r pct(a7b_med("hard_commitment_share", "anglophone_common"))` in anglophone countries and between `r pct(min(hard_other$median))` and `r pct(max(hard_other$median))` in the other four groups. Benefit-linked medians are closer, from `r pct(min(benefit_main$median))` to `r pct(max(benefit_main$median))`. Ranges within groups are wide: the hard-commitment share of anglophone countries runs from `r pct(val(a7b_groups, "min", measure == "hard_commitment_share", design_group == "anglophone_common"))` to `r pct(val(a7b_groups, "max", measure == "hard_commitment_share", design_group == "anglophone_common"))`.

```{r a7b-table}
a7b_show <- a7b_main %>%
  mutate(cell = paste0(pct(median), " [", round(100 * min), ", ", round(100 * max), "]"),
         group_label = paste0(design_labels[design_group], " (", n_countries, ")"),
         measure = measure_labels[measure]) %>%
  select(measure, group_label, cell) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = group_label, values_from = cell)

kable(a7b_show, col.names = c("Measure", names(a7b_show)[-1]), align = "lrrrrr",
      caption = "A7(b). Group median [min, max] of country shares, five main design groups (number of countries in brackets)")
```

Appendix Table A7(b) gives the country values and the median law year of each country.


# Robustness: social contributions and class placeholders

::: {.callout-note title="How to read this"}
**Social contributions** (pension and health-insurance contributions) are left out of the headline results; the second column adds them back. **Class placeholders** stand for classes of charges the law names without listing them; the third column drops them.

*Unit:* stated in each row. *Set:* headline = earmarked (assigned for A6), social contributions excluded. Shares are country-equal. Values are read from the saved `_sc` and `_nopl` tables.
:::

```{r robustness}
## The same measures, read from the three sets of saved tables
sets <- c(headline = "", sc = "_sc", nopl = "_nopl")
robust <- list()
for (s in names(sets)) {
  suffix <- sets[[s]]
  t_a1   <- read_table(paste0("02_A1_by_country", suffix))
  t_a2a  <- read_table(paste0("02_A2a_links", suffix))
  t_a2b  <- read_table(paste0("02_A2b_recipient_form", suffix))
  t_a3   <- read_table(paste0("02_A3_benefit_link", suffix)) %>% filter(group == "all countries")
  t_a4   <- read_table(paste0("04_A4_instrument", suffix)) %>% filter(group == "all countries")
  t_prof <- read_table(paste0("04_A7b_profile", suffix))
  t_a6   <- read_table(paste0("05_A6_subnational_by_country", suffix))

  ## Same columns as the headline tables, and the same 43 countries
  if (nrow(t_a1) != 43 || nrow(t_prof) != 43 || nrow(t_a6) != 43) stop("Robustness: not 43 countries in set ", s)
  ## The instrument-level shares of the profile are the country-equal means of A4 (same measure, two tables)
  if (abs(mean(t_prof$E3_share) - val(t_a4, "share_country_equal", category == "E3")) > 1e-9) stop("Robustness: E3 share differs between A4 and A7(b) in set ", s)
  if (abs(mean(t_prof$hard_commitment_share) - val(t_a4, "share_country_equal", category == "hard")) > 1e-9) stop("Robustness: hard share differs between A4 and A7(b) in set ", s)

  robust[[s]] <- tibble(
    measure = c("Earmarked instruments", "Restricted top-level allocations",
                "E3 (exclusive) share", "Hard-commitment share", "Fund-or-agency share", "Benefit-linked share",
                "704 Economic affairs, share of links",
                "A2b recipient forms: agency", "A2b recipient forms: fund",
                "A3 sectoral", "A3 unlinked", "A3 general revenue",
                "A6 sharing allocations", "A6 countries with any sharing"),
    unit = c("instrument", "allocation",
             "instrument", "instrument", "instrument", "link",
             "link",
             "allocation", "allocation",
             "link", "link", "link",
             "allocation (assigned set, retentions excluded)", "country"),
    kind = c("count", "count", rep("share", 10), "count", "count"),
    prose = c("", "", "E3 share", "hard-commitment share", "fund-or-agency share", "benefit-linked share",
              "704 share of links", "agency share of allocations", "fund share of allocations",
              "sectoral share of links", "unlinked share of links", "general revenue share of links", "", ""),
    value = c(sum(t_a1$n_earmarked), sum(t_a1$n_alloc_top_restricted),
              val(t_a4, "share_country_equal", category == "E3"),
              val(t_a4, "share_country_equal", category == "hard"),
              mean(t_prof$fund_agency_share),       # Table A1 measure: share of earmarked instruments
              mean(t_prof$benefit_linked_share),
              sum(t_a2a$share_country_equal[t_a2a$cofog_division == "704"]),
              val(t_a2b, "share_country_equal", recipient_form == "agency"),
              val(t_a2b, "share_country_equal", recipient_form == "fund"),
              val(t_a3, "share_country_equal", benefit_link == "sectoral"),
              val(t_a3, "share_country_equal", benefit_link == "unlinked"),
              val(t_a3, "share_country_equal", benefit_link == "general_revenue"),
              sum(t_a6$n_allocations), sum(t_a6$n_allocations > 0)),
    set = s)
}
robust <- bind_rows(robust) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = set, values_from = value)

## Largest change of a share against the headline set, in percentage points
robust_gap <- robust %>%
  filter(kind == "share") %>%
  pivot_longer(c(sc, nopl), names_to = "alt", values_to = "alt_value") %>%
  mutate(gap = abs(alt_value - headline)) %>%
  slice_max(gap, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
alt_labels <- c(sc = "with social contributions", nopl = "without class placeholders")

robust_show <- robust %>%
  mutate(across(c(headline, sc, nopl), ~ ifelse(kind == "share", pct(.x), num(.x)))) %>%
  select(measure, unit, headline, sc, nopl)

kable(robust_show, col.names = c("Measure", "Unit", "Headline", "Social contributions included", "Class placeholders excluded"),
      align = "llrrr", caption = "Robustness. Main values in the headline set and the two alternative sets (shares country-equal)")
```

Adding social contributions or dropping class placeholders changes no share in the table by more than `r round(100 * robust_gap$gap)` percentage points. The largest change is in the `r robust_gap$prose`, from `r pct(robust_gap$headline)` to `r pct(robust_gap$alt_value)` `r alt_labels[robust_gap$alt]`. The counts change more: the earmarked set holds `r num(val(robust, "sc", measure == "Earmarked instruments"))` instruments with social contributions and `r num(val(robust, "nopl", measure == "Earmarked instruments"))` without class placeholders, against `r num(val(robust, "headline", measure == "Earmarked instruments"))` in the headline set. Pooled shares, the other robustness check, are given next to the country-equal shares in each saved table.
